dedupe_keys.name: chicago city building footprint geojson release

description: The City of Chicago repository releases a transformed building-footprint layer and scripts that show how it was made from the city data portal. Its README says the portal’s original DBF and shapefile were cleaned of internal codes with OpenRefine and converted to GeoJSON with GDAL. The public tree lists a Buildings.zip archive, transformation files and Python, R and Ruby import examples. The repository’s own licence file grants MIT terms to this release. The original portal record was not resolved to a stable dataset identifier during this review, and the archive was not opened, so footprint count, geometry quality and observation date remain unverified. The README distinguishes this edited release from the portal data, which matters if a modeller needs exact provenance or fields omitted in cleaning. Simulation use includes building exposure overlays for a Chicago flood, heat or disruption scenario after checking coordinates and currency of the footprints. It complements data-nyc-building-footprints as a city-specific polygon source. The release documents conversion but does not itself establish present-day building stock.
licence: MIT for the City of Chicago repository release.
